Answer: F
Reason: The CT images demonstrate a large right pleural effusion with compressive atelectasis of the right lung, while the cardiac silhouette appears normal in size. In an elderly patient with increasing dyspnea and these specific findings (particularly if a chest X-ray showed a prominent left second arc suggesting a dilated pulmonary artery or anomalous vein), this presentation is characteristic of Scimitar syndrome (a congenital vascular anomaly involving partial anomalous pulmonary venous return), rather than heart failure or pneumonia.
